Section.Name: Residential Property
Section.Content:
Property owners are responsible for keeping their properties clean and free of pests.

To report New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) property, go to the NYCHA Public Housing Maintenance Complaint page instead.

What You Need

You must provide your contact information.

Indoors

You can report rodent conditions inside a residential apartment building.

Mice inside an apartment

Mice in a public area

Outdoors

You can report rodent conditions in outdoor areas of a residential property, including yards and alleys, to the NYC Health Department.

Rats inside a residential property

Section.Name: Food Establishment or Vendor
Section.Content:
You can report rats or mice in a restaurant or other place where food is served to the NYC Health Department. You can also report conditions that may attract them, like improper food or trash storage.

Types of food establishments include:

  • Bakery
  • Bar
  • Bodega
  • Café
  • Cafeteria or lunchroom
  • Deli
  • Restaurant
  • Soup kitchen

To report rats, mice, or droppings in food itself, go to the Food Safety Complaint page.

Section.Name: Food Retailer, Processor, or Warehouse
Section.Content:
You can report rats or mice or their droppings in places where food is sold, processed, or stored.

This includes retailers such as:

  • Grocery stores
  • Markets
  • Bodegas or convenience stores
  • Beverage stores

Section.Name: Rat or Mouse Complaint Vacant Building DOHMH SR
Section.Content:
Vacant Building

You can report rats or mice in an unoccupied building.

Dirty Vacant Lot

You can report a rodent condition on a vacant lot without any building or a building foundation, such as a concrete floor.

Owners of vacant lots are required to keep them clean and free of trash and debris.

You can report excessive trash and debris in a vacant lot that is attracting or may attract rats or mice to the Department of Sanitation (DSNY).

What You Need

Your report should describe:

  • The contents of the lot
  • If the lot is fenced or not

What Happens Next

The Department of Sanitation (DSNY) will inspect the lot. If the lot needs cleaning, DSNY will research the ownership of the property.

Then the NYC Health Department will give the owner a deadline to clean it. If the owner fails to meet the deadline, DSNY may clean the lot and charge the owner.

Vacant Lot Without Trash or Debris

You can report rats or mice in vacant lots that don’t contain trash or debris to the NYC Health Department.

Section.Name: Other Non-Residential Property
Section.Content:
You can report rats or mice on non-residential property to the NYC Health Department, such as:

  • Office buildings
  • Day cares or nurseries
  • Hospitals
  • Government property
  • Parking lots or garages
